<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines sources using standard AUR practices: it downloads a prebuilt .deb package from the project's own GitHub release page and a LICENSE file from the repository. The `source` and `sha256sums` arrays use parameter expansion with `_app` and `pkgver`, but these are simple string interpolations without command substitution or code execution. The top-level scope contains only safe variable assignments. The `pkgver()` function is absent, so no dynamic versioning occurs. There is no evidence of malicious code execution during sourcing, and the `prepare()` and `package()` functions are not executed due to `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`. The use of `noextract` is normal for binary packages. SKIPped checksums are not present; all sources have valid checksums. Fetching and extracting these sources is safe.
</details>
<summary>
Safe sourcing and source fetching
</summary>
</security_assessment>

The provided file is a standard `.desktop` file used for integrating applications into desktop environments on Linux systems. There is no evidence of malicious activity, data exfiltration, remote code execution, or supply chain tampering in this file. It serves purely as a launcher configuration and contains no logic beyond that.

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt `.deb` packages from the GitHub releases of the project's own upstream repository (https://github.com/zxcloli666/SoundCloud-Desktop) and extracts them using `bsdtar`. The sources are pinned to a specific version tag (`${pkgver}`), and SHA-256 checksums are provided for both `x86_64` and `aarch64` binaries, ensuring integrity. The build process (`prepare()` and `package()`) only involves unpacking the `.deb` archive and installing files into standard system directories (`/usr/bin`, `/usr/share/icons`, etc.), which is typical for a `-bin` package.

There are no network requests, dynamic downloads, or execution of remote code during build or install. No obfuscated commands, `eval`, or suspicious scripts are present. The use of `bsdtar` to extract Debian packages is standard practice in AUR binary packages. All operations are transparent and confined to the package's scope. While the package bypasses compilation (as expected for a `-bin` package), the source origins and checksums align with typical AUR packaging hygiene.

The `source` array references a `.desktop` file and `LICENSE` from the same GitHub repo, both at the tagged release, and these are also checksummed. No `git clone`, `curl | bash`, or other risky patterns are used. The maintainer uses standard AUR practices, and there is no evidence of supply-chain tampering or malicious behavior.
</details>
<summary>
Standard binary package with proper checksums and no malicious code
</summary>
</security_assessment>
